title: Backfill ghost graph from session moves
description: Existing production session_moves contain fen_before, move_san, and fen_after edges that were not copied into positions/moves. Build and run a reviewed backfill so historical play improves ghost steering coverage immediately, not only after new uploads.
design:
# Plan: Backfill ghost graph from historical session moves (g-backfill-graph)

## Context

`g-debug-ghost-steer` fixed the core bug: the ghost steering graph
(`positions` + `moves` tables) was never being taught from ordinary uploaded
games. The fix added `_upsert_session_position_graph()` in
`backend/app/api/session.py:303`, which validates each move with python-chess
(parse `move_san` on `fen_before`, push, compare normalized FEN to `fen_after`)
and inserts coherent `Position`/`Move` edges on every new upload.

That fix only helps **future** uploads. Production already holds many
`session_moves` rows with `fen_before` / `move_san` / `fen_after` that were never
copied into `positions`/`moves`. Ghost steering coverage stays poor until those
historical edges are backfilled. This task builds and runs a reviewed,
rerunnable backfill that applies the same validated insertion logic to existing
`session_moves`.

## Approach

Add a one-off script `backend/scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py`, modeled on the
existing `backend/scripts/recompute_srs_opportunities.py` (same arg-parsing,
`SessionLocal`, `_safe_database_url`, `--dry-run` conventions). It reuses the
production insertion logic rather than re-implementing it.

### Reuse the live function

`_upsert_session_position_graph(db, *, user_id, moves)` in
`backend/app/api/session.py` already does everything we need:
- validates each move's FEN coherence (`move_matches_fens`)
- creates/dedupes `Position` rows per `(user_id, fen_hash)`
- dedupes `Move` rows by `(from_position_id, move_san)` (the table PK), so
  re-running inserts nothing new — **idempotent / rerunnable**.

The function reads only `move.fen_before`, `move.fen_after`, `move.move_san`.
Stored `SessionMove` rows expose all three identically to `SessionMoveInput`, so
they can be passed directly (duck-typed). No refactor of the function is
required; if we want the type hint honest, optionally widen it to a small
`Protocol`, but that is not necessary.

### Script flow

1. Parse args: `--dry-run` (never commits), `--user-id` (optional, restrict to
   one user), `--limit` (cap sessions processed, for smoke runs),
   `--batch-size` (sessions per commit, default ~200), `--progress-every`.
2. Resolve `user_id` for each session by joining `session_moves` →
   `game_sessions.user_id` (SessionMove has only `session_id`).
3. Iterate **per user, per session**, ordered by session, then `move_number`,
   then **white before black** (explicit `color` ordering so an edge's
   `fen_before` is seen after the prior ply's `fen_after`). Group moves by
   `user_id` and call
   `_upsert_session_position_graph(db, user_id=uid, moves=session_moves_for_user)`.
   - Process per user so the function's in-memory `hash_to_position_id` cache and
     the `user_id` filter stay consistent (positions are user-scoped).
   - Only feed moves where both `fen_before` and `fen_after` are non-null
     (the function already skips otherwise, but filtering early is cheaper).
4. **Dry-run semantics (enforced):** when `dry_run=True` the script NEVER commits
   — batch commits are disabled entirely and a single `db.rollback()` runs at the
   end. When `dry_run=False`, commit per batch. Reported stats come from the
   counter object (step 5), never from before/after DB counts, so they are
   correct under both modes.
5. Accumulate counts from the counter object returned by the helper (see refactor
   below) and print a summary: sessions scanned, valid moves, invalid moves,
   positions created, edges created, edges already existing.

### Required refactor: counter return value

`_upsert_session_position_graph` currently returns `None`. Before/after DB row
deltas cannot distinguish *incoherent skips* from *valid duplicate edges*, and
are meaningless under per-batch-rollback dry runs. So make the helper return a
small counter (dataclass) tracking at least:
`valid_moves`, `invalid_moves`, `positions_created`, `edges_created`,
`edges_existing`. Update its two existing call sites in `upsert_session_moves`
(lines ~608, ~654) to ignore the return value. Single source of truth for counts;
behavior is otherwise unchanged.

### Required post-step: opportunity-event recompute

Graph backfill alone is not sufficient. `find_ghost_move`
(`backend/app/api/game.py:259`) consumes the graph, but ghost **eligibility**
switches to opportunity-counter mode whenever `BlunderOpportunityEvent` rows
exist (`_ghost_eligible` / `has_opportunity_events`,
`backend/app/api/game.py:225`). Historical events were computed before the graph
existed, so newly-reachable blunders can still be scored "not due." After the
graph backfill, the opportunity events must be recomputed via the fixed path in
`backend/scripts/recompute_srs_opportunities.py` (the work tracked in
`g-fix-srs-opps`, which now gates full recompute behind `--all-blunders` and
supports `--limit`).

Plan: add a `bd dep` so **g-backfill-graph depends on g-fix-srs-opps**, and make
the real-run checklist run graph backfill *then* the recompute script. (Decide
with the user whether the recompute is invoked by this script or run as a
separate documented step — see open question.)

### Production safety (races)

The helper does query-then-insert against the unique `(user_id, fen_hash)`
position constraint and the `(from_position_id, move_san)` move PK, so concurrent
live uploads during the backfill can hit uniqueness races. Mitigation, in
priority order: **run the backfill while API writes are paused/in a maintenance
window**; failing that, add conflict-tolerant insertion (catch
`IntegrityError`, rollback the failed unit, re-query and continue). At minimum,
the real-run checklist must state the pause requirement explicitly.

## Files

- **New:** `backend/scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py` — the backfill runner.
- **New:** `backend/test_backfill_ghost_graph.py` — tests (mirrors
  `test_rating_backfill.py` style).
- **Edit:** `backend/app/api/session.py` — counter return value on
  `_upsert_session_position_graph` (+ its two call sites).
- **Beads:** `bd dep add g-backfill-graph g-fix-srs-opps`.

## Tests

In `backend/test_backfill_ghost_graph.py`, using the existing in-memory/sqlite
test DB fixtures from `test_session_api.py` / `conftest.py`:

1. **Happy path:** seed a `game_session` + several coherent `session_moves` with
   no pre-existing `positions`/`moves`; run backfill; assert the expected
   `Position` rows (by `user_id`+`fen_hash`) and `Move` edges exist.
2. **Incoherent move skipped:** seed a move whose `move_san` does not transform
   `fen_before` into `fen_after`; assert no graph edge is created (mirrors the
   existing `test_session_moves_skip_invalid_ghost_graph_edge`).
3. **Idempotent rerun:** run twice; assert second run creates zero new rows.
4. **Dry-run:** assert `--dry-run` leaves `positions`/`moves` unchanged.
5. **User scoping:** two users with identical FENs produce distinct, user-scoped
   `Position` rows.

## Verification

All commands require the venv:

- `cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest test_backfill_ghost_graph.py test_session_api.py -q`
- Smoke / dry run against a real DB snapshot:
  `cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py --dry-run --limit 50`
  and review the printed counter summary (valid/invalid moves, positions/edges
  created, edges existing). Confirm nothing was committed.
- Spot-check a known user: confirm `positions`/`moves` counts increase and that
  ghost steering now finds due-blunder continuations for historical positions.

## Real-run checklist

1. **Pause API writes** (maintenance window) to avoid uniqueness races, unless
   conflict-tolerant insertion was implemented.
2. Run graph backfill: `... && python scripts/backfill_ghost_graph.py`
   (record the counter summary in the bead).
3. Run the opportunity recompute (g-fix-srs-opps path):
   `... && python scripts/recompute_srs_opportunities.py --all-blunders`.
4. Resume API writes.
5. Record before/after `positions`/`moves` counts in the bead; close per the
   session-close protocol.

title: Drill 'Another drill' button does nothing after mid-board stop
description: When a drill stops mid-board (off_route/accuracy → drillState='failed'), DrillStopActions renders with isGameActive=true. Clicking 'Another drill' calls handleNewDrillSticky which sets showStartOverlay(true) but intentionally keeps isGameActive=true (so handleNewDrill's abandon guard fires on start). However the start overlay in BoardStage only renders when 'showStartOverlay && !isGameActive', so the overlay never appears and nothing happens.
design: Fix: render the start overlay over a stopped drill by changing BoardStage condition to 'showStartOverlay && (!isGameActive || isStoppedDrill)' and threading isStoppedDrill prop through. Keeps isGameActive=true so handleNewDrill's abandon guard still abandons the failed session when the new drill starts (handleNewDrill sets showStartOverlay(false) on success).

title: Drill fails immediately on suboptimal opening first move
description: Selecting an opening whose first move is not the engine's global best move (e.g. Polish 1.b4 vs 1.e4) ends the drill immediately during pre-root steering with 'That move exceeds the allowed centipawn loss.' Cause: the pre-root accuracy check compares the played move against the engine's GLOBAL best move, so any deliberately-suboptimal opening route move fails. Decision: exempt on-route moves from the accuracy/cp check entirely; pre-root only fails on off_route. Accuracy check is in 3 places: drills.py route-check, session.py move-upload (_maybe_fail_active_drill_on_accuracy), and ChessGame.tsx analysis listener.
notes: Fix: exempt on-route moves from the centipawn/accuracy check during pre-root steering. title: Gate ghost SRS by actual reach probability
description:
Normal ghost mode can keep targeting blunders that have many ancestor-radius opportunity events but
almost no actual reaches. Example: blunder 578 had opportunities_since_review=183,
opportunities_30d=183, reached_30d=0, p_reach=0.0107, yet /api/game/next-opponent-move returned it
as target_blunder_id from decision_source=ghost_path. This makes the player repeat steering into a
bad branch after they appear to have learned to avoid that branch.

Observed API case:

Request FEN: rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/1P6/5N2/PBPPPPPP/RN1QKB1R b KQkq - 1 3
Moves: b2b4, e7e6, c1b2, d7d5, g1f3
Response selected ghost move c7c5 and target_blunder_id=578
SRS fields: last_reviewed_at=null, pass_count=0, fail_count=0, pass_streak=0,
opportunities_since_review=183, opportunities_30d=183, reached_30d=0, p_reach=0.0107

Implementation trace:

backend/app/api/session.py computes opportunity events when the session reaches the blunder position
or any reverse ancestor within OPPORTUNITY_ANCESTOR_RADIUS_PLY.
backend/app/api/game.py builds GhostMoveCandidate with opportunity counters.
The eligibility gate at find_ghost_move uses
calculate_opportunity_overdue(opportunities_since_review, pass_streak) when opportunity events exist.
backend/app/srs_math.py calculate_opportunity_overdue is raw opportunities_since_review /
expected_opportunities(pass_streak).
p_reach is only applied later inside GhostMoveCandidate.score as compute_p_reach(reached_30d,
opportunities_30d) ** OPPORTUNITY_POWER.
Therefore p_reach lowers score but does not determine eligibility. A low-reach blunder can still be
selected when it is the only eligible candidate or when other candidates score lower.

Option evaluation:

1 Weight the gate by opportunities_since_review * p_reach / expected_opportunities. This is a low-
risk first step, but insufficient alone. In the example, 183 * 0.0107 = 1.96, so a pass-streak-0
blunder still passes the >= 1 gate.
2 Add a p_reach floor. This directly fixes the symptom. Use only after enough samples to avoid hiding
sparse data, for example opportunities_30d >= 30 and p_reach < 0.03 or 0.05. Risk: hard threshold
can hide rare but important lines from normal ghost mode.
3 Use reached_since_review as the overdue signal. This is the best conceptual balance. Normal SRS
urgency should come from positions the player actually reaches. Ancestor opportunities should inform
probability and scoring, not by themselves force steering into avoided branches. Requires adding a
reached_since_review counter to load_opportunity_counters.
4 Suppress until actually reached once. This is strongest against repetition but too aggressive as
the whole policy. Good for normal ghost mode only if explicit drill/review can still surface old
blunders.

Recommendation:

Implement option 3 as the core rule for normal ghost eligibility: due when reached_since_review /
expected_opportunities(pass_streak) >= 1.
Add option 2 as a guarded backstop: when opportunities_30d is sufficiently large and p_reach is
extremely low, skip the blunder in normal ghost steering.
Keep explicit review/drill flows able to surface these blunders by time/severity even when normal
ghost mode suppresses them.

Acceptance criteria:

load_opportunity_counters exposes reached_since_review.
normal ghost eligibility for candidates with opportunity events uses reached_since_review, not raw
opportunities_since_review, as the overdue gate.
a candidate like blunder 578 with 183 opportunities, 0 reaches, and p_reach around 0.01 is not
selected by normal ghost steering solely because of ancestor opportunities.
explicit drill/review endpoints still have a path to review low-reach blunders.
tests cover low-reach high-opportunity suppression, reached-since-review eligibility, and
preservation of intentional review/drill behavior.
design:
## Implementation Plan

### Core change (Option 3): reached_since_review as eligibility gate

**srs_opportunity.py**

Add `reached_since_review: int = 0` to `OpportunityCounters` dataclass.

Add SQL condition in `load_opportunity_counters` parallel to `opportunity_since_review` but filtered to `reached=True`:
```python
reached_since_review = and_(
    BlunderOpportunityEvent.reached.is_(True),
    event_after_blunder_created,
    or_(
        latest_review.c.reviewed_at.is_(None),
        and_(
            BlunderOpportunityEvent.session_id != latest_review.c.session_id,
            event_time > latest_review.c.reviewed_at,
        ),
    ),
)
```
Add to SELECT and row construction.

Do NOT change opportunity_priority() (line 138) — keeps using opportunities_since_review so /api/blunder listing still surfaces low-reach blunders for explicit review. Converted drills call find_ghost_move normally so normal suppression applies; the preservation path is /api/blunder?due=true.

---

**game.py**

Add constants:
```python
P_REACH_FLOOR = 0.03
P_REACH_MIN_SAMPLE = 30
```
Calibration: with Laplace smoothing (reached+2)/(opp+4), P_REACH_FLOOR=0.03 only triggers at ~63+ opp with 0 reaches. P_REACH_MIN_SAMPLE=30 is intentionally conservative. Backstop is defense-in-depth; primary fix is reached_since_review gate.

Add `reached_since_review: int = 0` to GhostMoveCandidate.

Extract `_ghost_eligible` helper (instead of keeping gate + backstop inline) to give unit-testable surface:
```python
def _ghost_eligible(
    *,
    has_opportunity_events: bool,
    reached_since_review: int,
    pass_streak: int,
    last_reviewed_at: datetime | None,
    created_at: datetime | None,
    now: datetime,
    opportunities_30d: int,
    reached_30d: int,
) -> bool:
    if has_opportunity_events:
        priority = calculate_opportunity_overdue(
            opportunities_since_review=reached_since_review,
            pass_streak=pass_streak,
        )
    else:
        priority = calculate_priority(pass_streak=pass_streak, last_reviewed_at=last_reviewed_at, created_at=created_at, now=now)
    if priority < 1.0:
        return False
    if (
        has_opportunity_events
        and opportunities_30d >= P_REACH_MIN_SAMPLE
        and compute_p_reach(reached_30d, opportunities_30d) < P_REACH_FLOOR
    ):
        return False
    return True
```

Replace inline gate in find_ghost_move (~line 337) with a call to _ghost_eligible.

Update GhostMoveCandidate.score() urgency for opportunity candidates:
```python
if self.has_opportunity_events:
    urgency = calculate_opportunity_overdue(
        opportunities_since_review=self.reached_since_review,  # was: self.opportunities_since_review
        pass_streak=self.pass_streak,
    )
```

Pass `reached_since_review=counters.reached_since_review if counters else 0` in candidate construction.

---

### Tests

**test_srs_opportunity.py — unit tests for reached_since_review**
- reached_since_review=0 when 183 opp events but 0 exact reaches
- Counts only reaches since last review; excludes review-session reach and pre-review reaches

**DB integration test (test_srs_opportunity.py or test_game_api.py)**
- Build DB scenario: blunder reachable via ghost path, 183 ancestor-only events, 0 exact reaches
- find_ghost_move returns (None, None, None, None) — not selected despite high opportunities_since_review

**test_srs_priority.py — unit tests against _ghost_eligible helper**
- Threshold: reached_since_review=1, pass_streak=0 → priority=1.0, filter is < 1.0 so 1.0 IS eligible
- reached_since_review=0 → priority=0.0 → not eligible
- reached_since_review=2 → priority=2.0 → eligible
- Backstop fires: opportunities_30d=183, reached_30d=0 → p_reach≈0.011 < 0.03 → not eligible
- Backstop does not fire at opportunities_30d=20 (below sample floor)
- Backstop does not fire when p_reach >= 0.03
- Backstop does not fire when has_opportunity_events=False

**test_blunder_list_api.py — explicit review still available**
- Blunder with opportunities_since_review=183, reached_since_review=0 still appears in GET /api/blunder?due=true
- Confirms opportunity_priority() in srs_opportunity.py:138 is unchanged

---

title: Split /game board state from sidebar and analysis state
description: The /game screen keeps board interaction state, move history, graph state, opening lookup, review UI, and post-game UI in one large top-level component. Isolate the live board path so worker and sidebar updates do not rerender board-critical logic during dragging.
design:
## V1 Plan

### Approach
Split rendering first, introduce zustand only for cross-boundary shared state. Keep Chess instance, async effects, and most derived values outside the store.

### Step 1: Split ChessGame into BoardContainer + SidebarContainer
- BoardContainer props: fen, viewIndex, playerColor, boardOrientation, drag eligibility inputs, square highlights (selectedSquare, optionSquares, lastMoveSquares), board-local overlays (showFlash, showRevertWarning, showRehookToast, start/end overlays)
- analysisMap, streamingEval, and move-list data stay entirely out of BoardContainer
- SidebarContainer: moveHistory, viewIndex, analysisMap, streamingEval, blunderAlert, blunderReview*, moveMessages, liveOpening, showPostGamePrompt, gameResult, ratingChange
- ChessGame becomes a thin shell wiring the two containers
- Derive cheap values (displayedFen, allowDragging, squareStyles, blunderArrows) in subscriber components or selectors, NOT stored

### Step 2: Extract EvalBar from BoardStage
- selectedEvalCp changes during live analysis will almost certainly cause board rerenders
- Cheap split — extract EvalBar into its own subscriber component outside BoardStage
- Profile to confirm, but expect this to be needed

### Step 3: Introduce zustand for hot cross-boundary state
Canonical state in the store:
- **Session**: sessionId, isGameActive, gameResult, playerColor, playerColorChoice, boardOrientation, engineElo, isRated, playerRating, ratingChange
- **Game position**: One authoritative live position (liveFen — the actual board position from the game engine) + navigation state (moveHistory, viewIndex). displayedFen is derived: if viewIndex points to history use moveHistory[viewIndex].fen, otherwise use liveFen. Never store displayedFen — always derive it.
- engineStatus/isThinking stay in their existing hooks initially
- Chess.js instance: controller object owned by the page/session (not a bare module singleton), so tests and potential future multi-board views can coexist. Store actions consume results from the controller, never mutate chess state directly.

Design constraints:
- playerColor in session slice, not board
- allowDragging is derived, don't store
- Keep overlay flags separate
- No computed-on-write unless proven expensive
- No mutable objects in zustand state
- Effects stay in hooks, not store subscribers

### Step 4: Refactor controller/lifecycle hooks
- Migrate useChessGameController, useOpponentMove, useChessGameLifecycle to use store.getState() for cross-boundary state
- Remove refs that existed only for stale-closure workarounds
- Keep effects in dedicated hooks subscribing to narrow store selectors, colocated by concern:
  - Review/blunder effects (blunder detection, SRS grading, review moment)
  - Opening lookup effect
  - Toast/timer effects (flash dismiss, toast dismiss, alert dismiss)
notes:
## Verification Checklist
- [ ] React DevTools Profiler before/after (ask Miguel to run DevTools at checkpoint)
- [ ] Confirm BoardContainer does NOT re-render on streamingEval updates alone
- [ ] Confirm piece drag remains smooth during opponent analysis
- [ ] No regressions in: revert flow, move navigation, blunder review, ghost moves, postgame transitions

title: Spike: Maia-2 runtime feasibility (browser vs backend engine service)
description:
## Summary
Investigate and decide where Maia-2 inference should run for Ghost Replay.

Primary question:
Can we run Maia-2 directly in-browser (similar to current Stockfish WASM workers), or should we re-architect to run Maia-2 on the backend and expose an engine API?

## Why This Child Issue Exists
Parent issue `ghostreplay-29c` defines a continuous Maia-2 difficulty slider. That work is blocked until we resolve runtime placement (browser vs backend), because the integration surface, latency budget, and infra costs differ significantly.

## Current Findings (as of 2026-02-06)
### Upstream Maia-2 implementation reality
From `CSSLab/maia2` (HEAD `16c138306339b87215abc8de45ac47c50ec603b1`, 2025-07-23):
- Official package is Python-first (`pip install maia2`), with examples in Python only.
- Dependencies include `torch==2.4.0`, `gdown`, `numpy`, `pandas`, etc. (not a JS/browser runtime stack).
- `model.from_pretrained(type, device)` downloads `.pt` checkpoints via Google Drive URLs and loads via `torch.load(...)`.
- API supports only `type in {"rapid", "blitz"}` checkpoints.
- Elo input is bucketized in code (`<1100`, 100-point bins 1100-1999, `>=2000`), not truly continuous.

### Implication
There is no official browser/WASM/JS inference path in `maia2` today; direct frontend drop-in appears non-trivial and likely requires model export + runtime porting work.

## Ghost Replay Architectural Context
- Current app runs engine logic in browser workers via `stockfish.wasm` (`src/workers/stockfishWorker.ts`, `src/workers/analysisWorker.ts`).
- Backend currently coordinates session/ghost data and does not run chess engine inference (`backend/app/api/game.py`).
- If Maia-2 cannot be made practical client-side, engine responsibility must move server-side (or hybrid), which changes API boundaries and operational requirements.

## Scope of This Spike
1. Validate browser feasibility concretely
- Determine whether a realistic browser path exists without training a new model:
  - export/conversion requirements (e.g., ONNX/TorchScript/WebGPU runtime),
  - expected model size/load time,
  - browser memory/compute viability on target devices,
  - dependency/licensing constraints for shipping weights.

2. Produce backend fallback design (if browser is not viable)
- Define API contract for engine inference endpoint(s), including request/response schema.
- Define move-selection contract needed by parent continuous-slider work (Maia probs + judge metrics + chosen move).
- Define execution model: sync request, async queue, or streaming.
- Define caching strategy for model load and prepared inference artifacts.
- Define deployment assumptions (CPU baseline, optional GPU), throughput targets, and cost risks.

3. Recommend architecture decision
- Provide explicit go/no-go for browser runtime.
- If no-go: provide phased migration plan for backend engine integration.

## Deliverables
- Decision memo in repo docs (`docs/maia2-runtime-feasibility.md`) with evidence and recommendation.
- Proposed API spec for engine inference endpoint(s).
- Initial implementation plan (milestones + estimates) for selected architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Browser feasibility is tested and documented with concrete technical blockers or validated path.
- A clear architectural decision is recorded: `browser`, `backend`, or `hybrid`, with rationale.
- If decision is backend/hybrid, a concrete API contract and migration plan are documented.
- Parent issue `ghostreplay-29c` is updated with dependency outcome and next actionable tasks.

## Non-Goals
- Implementing full Maia-2 production inference in this issue.
- Full Elo calibration or continuous-slider tuning logic (covered by parent and follow-on tasks).

## References
- Upstream repo: https://github.com/CSSLab/maia2
- Parent: `ghostreplay-29c`

title: Backend: Implement SRS priority calculation
description:
Implement the SRS priority scoring used for Ghost steering selection.

**SRS priority (overdue-ness):**
```
expected_interval = BASE_INTERVAL * (BACKOFF_FACTOR ^ pass_streak)
hours_since_review = (NOW - last_reviewed_at) in hours
srs_priority = hours_since_review / expected_interval
```

A blunder is **due** when srs_priority > 1.0.

**Selection score (used by scent CTE):**
```
score = srs_priority * (eval_loss_cp / 50) / (1 + 0.1 * distance)
```

- eval_loss_cp/50: severity weight (200cp blunder scores 4x vs 50cp inaccuracy)
- 1/(1+0.1*distance): distance tiebreaker within 5-move steering radius

**Constants:**
- BASE_INTERVAL = 1 hr
- BACKOFF_FACTOR = 2.0
- MAX_INTERVAL = 4320 hrs (180 days cap)
- STEERING_RADIUS = 5
- RECORDING_MOVE_CAP = 10
notes:
Refinement proposals from design discussion:

1) Bound/saturating overdue variant (time-based):

```
overdue = hours_since / expected_interval
urgency = 1 + log2(1 + overdue)          # or clamp
severity = log1p(eval_loss_cp / 50)
distance_weight = exp(-0.35 * distance)
score = urgency * severity * distance_weight
```

2) Selection stochasticity:
- Sample from top-k candidates (not always top-1) to improve variety and avoid repetitive steering.

3) Opportunity-aware scoring (preferred for branch explosion):

```
opp_overdue = opportunities_since_review / expected_opportunities(pass_streak)
severity = log1p(eval_loss_cp / 50)
distance_weight = 1 / (1 + 0.1 * distance)

p_reach = (reached_30d + 2) / (opportunities_30d + 4)   # smoothed
opening_weight = 1.0 (same opening family) else 0.1      # or 0 in strict mode

score = opp_overdue * severity * distance_weight * (p_reach ^ 1.5) * opening_weight
```

4) Scope note:
- Do not add opening-family gating as a separate optional mode in this ticket.
Implementation progress (2026-02-11):
- Updated ghost traversal scoring in backend/app/api/game.py to compute and rank candidates by:
  score = srs_priority * (eval_loss_cp / 50.0) / (1 + 0.1 * depth)
- Enforced steering radius at depth <= 5 in recursive CTE (parameterized).
- Added shared SRS math module (backend/app/srs_math.py) and reused it in /api/srs/review and ghost scoring path.
- Added/updated tests for depth cap and score preferences (severity and overdue priority).

Open follow-up for this ticket:
- The bounded-overdue variant, top-k sampling, and opportunity-aware scoring from notes are not yet implemented in code.

- Section 6.1 (Scent Logic) assumes a connected graph from start to blunder

title: Graph model claimed as DAG but chess graphs have cycles
description:
## Problem

The spec explicitly calls the graph model a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)**, but chess graphs naturally have cycles.

In real chess, repetition is common (threefolds, perpetual checks, transpositions that revisit positions), so cycles can appear as soon as the same normalized FEN is re-reached.

While a standard chess game moves forward in time (making it seem acyclic), the database stores **Positions (FENs)**. In chess, it is perfectly valid to reach the same position twice (e.g., 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. Ng1 Ng8). If a user has ever practiced a "draw by repetition" line, the graph will contain a physical loop (Node A → Node B → Node A).

## Spec Correction Needed

Update SPEC.md to:
1. Clarify the graph is a **directed graph with potential cycles**, not a true DAG
2. Document that recursive queries require depth bounds and cycle detection
3. Include the recommended query pattern below

## Recommended Query Pattern (for spec)

PostgreSQL 14+ has a built-in CYCLE detection feature. For older versions, use depth counter + path tracking:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE scent_path AS (
    -- BASE CASE: Starting moves from current position
    SELECT 
        m.from_position_id,
        m.to_position_id,
        m.move_san AS root_move,
        1 AS depth,
        ARRAY[m.from_position_id] as path_history
    FROM moves m
    JOIN positions p ON p.id = m.from_position_id
    WHERE p.fen_hash = :current_fen_hash

    UNION ALL

    -- RECURSIVE STEP
    SELECT 
        child.from_position_id,
        child.to_position_id,
        parent.root_move,
        parent.depth + 1,
        parent.path_history || child.from_position_id
    FROM moves child
    JOIN scent_path parent ON parent.to_position_id = child.from_position_id
    WHERE 
        parent.depth < 15                                          -- Depth limit
        AND NOT (child.to_position_id = ANY(parent.path_history))  -- Cycle detection
)
SELECT 
    root_move, 
    COUNT(*) as distinct_blunders,
    MIN(depth) as closest_blunder_distance,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.srs_due_date <= NOW() THEN 10 ELSE 1 END) as urgency_score
FROM scent_path sp
JOIN positions p ON p.id = sp.to_position_id
WHERE p.is_blunder = TRUE
GROUP BY root_move
ORDER BY urgency_score DESC, closest_blunder_distance ASC
LIMIT 1;
```

**Key safeguards:**
- `depth < 15`: Hard cap prevents runaway recursion (blunders 20+ moves away have "faint scent" anyway)
- `path_history` array + `NOT ... = ANY(...)`: Prevents infinite loops from 3-fold repetition patterns
close_reason: Updated SPEC.md: corrected DAG terminology to 'directed graph with potential cycles', added cycle detection and depth bound requirements, included reference SQL implementation with safeguards

**Category: SPEC.md Update Required**

- interval = interval * ease_factor
- ease_factor adjusts per item

- Fixed box intervals: [1, 3, 7, 14, 30] days
- Simpler, more predictable

```
On PASS: interval = max(1, interval * ease_factor), ease_factor += 0.1
On FAIL: interval = 1, ease_factor = max(1.5, ease_factor - 0.2)
Initial: interval=0, ease_factor=2.5
Cap: interval <= 180 days
```

- Maximum interval cap?

```sql
CREATE TABLE blunders (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id BIGINT REFERENCES users(id),
    position_id BIGINT REFERENCES positions(id),
    user_move_san VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,

);
```

## Design Decision
This separates the graph structure (positions/moves) from user-specific blunder tracking. Same position can be a blunder for multiple users with different SRS schedules.

title: Store blunder context (wrong move, best move, eval delta)
description:
Currently the schema only marks `is_blunder=TRUE` on positions but doesn't store the context needed to explain the mistake to the user.

## Problem
When reviewing a blunder, we need to show:
- 'You played Qxd4' (the mistake)
- 'Nf3 was better' (the correction)
- 'This lost 3.5 pawns of advantage' (the severity)

## Schema Changes

```sql
CREATE TABLE blunders (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id BIGINT REFERENCES users(id),
    position_id BIGINT REFERENCES positions(id),
    
    -- The mistake
    user_move_san VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,    -- e.g., 'Qxd4'
    user_move_eval INTEGER,                 -- centipawns after user move
    
    -- The correction
    best_move_san VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,    -- e.g., 'Nf3'
    best_move_eval INTEGER,                 -- centipawns after best move
    
    -- Derived
    eval_delta INTEGER,                     -- best - user (positive = blunder)
    
    -- SRS (move from positions table)
    srs_due_date TIMESTAMP,
    srs_interval INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    srs_ease_factor FLOAT DEFAULT 2.5,
    
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

## Benefits
- SRS data is now per-user (same position, different users)
- Can show detailed feedback during review
- Can track severity trends over time

title: Reclaim vertical space to grow board in /play 2-col breakpoint
description: In the max-width:1099px 2-column layout, the board should grow as viewport height shrinks. All board sizing flows through the --game-board-max-width max() formula in App.css:2066, which subtracts --game-viewport-chrome, --game-graph-height, and 1rem. Lever: shrink the fixed 220px graph via a dvh-based clamp, plus optional height-scoped chrome reduction. Constraint: bottom row is 'graph panel' side-by-side so row height = max(graph, panel); panel height is the floor.
design:
# Keep the analysis graph in view on short viewports (/play 2-col)

Bead: **g-9g1y**

## Context

In `/play`'s middle-width **2-column** layout (`@media (max-width: 1099px)`, down to 660px), the
analysis graph is a fixed **220px** (`--game-graph-height`, `src/App.css:2065`). All board sizing
flows through one formula (`src/App.css:2066`):

```css
--game-board-max-width: max(300px,
  calc(100dvh - var(--game-viewport-chrome) - var(--game-graph-height) - 1rem));
```

The 2-col grid is:

```
"board moves"
"graph panel"   /* .has-graph */
```

Because the board is sized as `100dvh − chrome − graph − 1rem`, **board + graph fit the usable
height by construction** — until the board hits its `max(300px, …)` floor. On short viewports the
board bottoms out at 300px, can't yield more, and the fixed 220px graph gets pushed **below the
fold around 680px tall**. That's the problem to fix.

### User priorities (confirmed)
1. **Graph must stay above the fold** — strong preference. Target: keep it fully visible **down to
   ~600px** viewport height (today it drops off ~680px).
2. **Panel may fall below the fold** (page scroll) — acceptable, *provided* warning messages remain
   visible. Warnings are the critical in-game info.
3. **Do not shrink the panel further.**

### Why this is the graph lever, done right (resolves earlier review)
A prior draft tied the graph's clamp floor to the panel height to avoid scroll. That was wrong:
`.chess-panel` (`App.css:2106`) is a `flex-column gap:1rem` stacking status + a ~70px avatar matchup
+ material + warnings, so it routinely exceeds 220px and grows with warnings. But priority #2 says
the **panel is allowed to overflow**, so we *don't* keep it in view and *don't* tie the floor to it.
The graph floor is set purely by the "graph in view at ~600px" goal.

**Warnings stay visible for free:** the board reserves the (now smaller) graph height for row 2, so
row 2's *top* sits above the fold by ~one graph-height. The warning stack is already pinned to the
panel top via `order:-1` (`App.css:7584`), so it lands above the fold while the rest of the panel
scrolls off — exactly "shows warning messages on top." No new warning UI, no panel changes.

## Approach

### Step 1 — Viewport-proportional graph height (the change)
"Proportional to the board" is circular (board depends on graph). Break it by tying the graph to the
**independent** variable, viewport height, scoped **inside the existing 2-col media query** so
desktop 3-col is untouched:

```css
@media (max-width: 1099px) {
  .chess-layout {
    --game-graph-height: clamp(110px, 20dvh, 220px);
  }
}
```

- `20dvh`: hits the 220px cap at ~1100px tall; shrinks below that.
- `110px` floor: keeps the graph in view at the ~600px target (math below) and readable.
- The graph SVG already binds to the variable (`App.css:2501`) — no other rule changes.

Tunable: floor/ratio are the two knobs; verify against the 600px target before finalizing.

### Step 2 — Reconcile the short-height chrome bumps
`--game-viewport-chrome` jumps to `6.5rem` at `max-height:760` and `8.5rem` at `max-height:680`
(`App.css:5194`/`5200`), which *shrinks the board to fit the fixed 220px graph* — partly redundant
now that the graph shrinks. **Verify** whether these still over-shrink the board (wasted space); if
so, relax them in a `.game-page`-scoped rule. **Per review:** any such override must be declared
**after** the `max-height` blocks (after `App.css:5204`) so source order + specificity win — do not
edit them in place earlier. Treat as verify-then-maybe-trim, not a guaranteed edit.

### Files to modify
- `src/App.css` — add the `--game-graph-height` clamp inside `@media (max-width: 1099px)` (near
  `7556`); optional Step-2 chrome override placed after `5204`.
- No JS/TSX changes. No panel changes. Reuses `--game-graph-height` / `--game-board-max-width` / the
  SVG rule at `2501` / the `order:-1` warning pin at `7584`.

## Corrected goal & sizing (addresses review #2, #3)

**Goal wording:** *not* "board grows as height shrinks" (false — board ≈ `0.8·vh − chrome` still
shrinks with vh). Correct: **"the graph stays fully above the fold down to ~600px (vs ~680px today),
and the board is larger than today's board at the same short height."**

Board **vertical budget** = `--game-board-max-width` (the wrapper max-width). Caveats: above 767px
the square is the wrapper **minus the eval bar** `2rem + 0.4rem` (`App.css:2510`/`2522`); the
horizontal grid track (`minmax(0,1fr)`) can cap the square independently of height; and `max(300px,…)`
floors the value.

| vh | chrome | graph (20dvh→clamp) | today budget `max(300, vh−chrome−220−16)` | new budget `max(300, vh−chrome−graph−16)` | graph in view? |
|----|--------|----|----|----|----|
| 800 | 72 (4.5rem) | 160 | 492 | 552 | today ✓ / new ✓ |
| 760 | 104 (6.5rem) | 152 | 420 | 488 | ✓ / ✓ |
| 680 | 136 (8.5rem) | 136 | 308 | 392 | ✓ (edge) / ✓ |
| 600 | 136 (8.5rem) | 120 | **300 (floored; real 228 → overflow)** | 328 | **today ✗ (falls off)** / new ✓ |

At 600px today the budget floors at 300 while only 228px exists → overflow pushes the graph off; the
clamp keeps the graph at 120px and in view. Numbers are the vertical budget only; apply the eval-bar
and horizontal caveats above for the actual square.

## Verification (addresses review #5)
JSDOM/`breakpoints.test.ts` only guards the 659/660 constant and can't validate layout. Add focused
**Playwright geometry** checks (mid-game *and* warning state) asserting:
- graph element's bottom ≤ viewport bottom (in view) and the warning stack is within the viewport;

title: Persist stronger analysis-board evals
description:
## Problem
In-game Stockfish WASM analysis currently uses a weaker depth-17 single-PV search, while the analysis board runs a stronger depth-21 MultiPV search. Analysis-board results are transient, so stronger evidence cannot improve analysis_cache and weaker game evaluations may remain the durable value. More generally, the application needs reusable profile ordering so convenient weaker searches can populate missing keys without preventing later stronger compatible searches from upgrading them.

## Objective
Allow complete, compatible analysis evidence produced on the analysis board or by future stronger searches to be persisted through the shared analysis-cache writer and replace weaker compatible evidence according to explicit profile dominance.

## Scope
- Define exact immutable browser search profiles for in-game depth-17 analysis and analysis-board depth-21 MultiPV analysis, including pinned WASM/build identity, search settings, and analyzer protocol.
- Extend profile comparison to express explicit stronger/weaker relationships without inferring a universal ordering from raw depth.
- Separate trusted replacement eligibility from canonical trusted-hit/legacy-reclamation authority so a stronger browser profile can replace a weaker browser profile without becoming equivalent to native canonical precompute.
- Add an authenticated batch endpoint for writing approved analysis evidence through write_analysis_cache_rows; the backend validates or stamps the allowed producer profile rather than trusting arbitrary client authority claims.
- Convert completed unrestricted analysis-board searches into complete evidence rows and persist them.
- When the played move is not represented by the unrestricted MultiPV result, run the required targeted search so played_eval, best_eval, eval_delta, classification, best move, and best PV come from a coherent profile and satisfy the evidence contract.
- Preserve the canonical depth-24 profile over browser depth-21 evidence.
- Keep incompatible engine builds, networks, search-limit types, protocols, and restricted/hybrid searches unordered and unable to overwrite one another.
- Add diagnostics for accepted/rejected upgrades and tests for profile ordering, endpoint validation, evidence construction, and analysis-board persistence.

## Important Edge Case
AnalysisBoard currently may exclude the cached best move with searchmoves and merge the old cached line into live depth-21 lines for display. That hybrid result must not be stamped as a coherent depth-21 profile or persisted as replacement evidence. Cache-producing analysis must use an unrestricted search to establish the best line and a compatible targeted played-move search when needed.

## Non-Goals
- Do not rewrite historical session_moves when cache evidence improves.
- Do not treat numeric depth alone as a cross-engine quality score.
- Do not allow browser evidence to replace the native canonical depth-24 profile or reclaim unidentified legacy rows merely because its depth is higher than another browser search.
- Do not change live indexed-move source arbitration owned by g-cache-first-resolve.

## Existing Foundation
g-guard-cache-writes is complete and already provides analysis profile metadata, evidence contracts, the deterministic comparator, and the shared transaction-safe writer. This issue extends that foundation; it is not blocked on the completed bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A complete approved depth-21 analysis-board profile replaces a complete depth-17 browser-game row for the same (fen_before, move_uci).
2. Depth-17 browser evidence cannot replace depth-21 analysis-board evidence.
3. Neither browser profile replaces an active canonical depth-24 row.
4. Incompatible or unidentified profiles remain unordered and cannot overwrite trusted evidence.
5. Numeric depth is never used as a generic cross-profile comparator; ordering is explicit and deterministic.
6. Browser profile metadata is validated or stamped by the backend, and clients cannot claim arbitrary canonical or authoritative identities.
7. Only coherent completed analysis is persisted; restricted searchmoves plus a merged cached line is rejected as cache-producing evidence.
8. Persisted rows satisfy the complete evidence contract, including best move/PV, played and best evaluations, eval_delta, and classification.
9. Played moves outside the unrestricted MultiPV result receive a compatible targeted evaluation before persistence.
10. All writes route through write_analysis_cache_rows and expose accepted/rejected reason diagnostics.
11. Tests cover upgrade/downgrade/canonical/incompatible ordering, endpoint validation, score perspective and mate handling, targeted played-move evaluation, interrupted searches, and duplicate submissions.
12. SPEC.md documents browser profile ordering and analysis-board cache persistence.

title: Mobile portrait: reclaim vertical space to bring analysis graph into view
description: On /play mobile portrait (max-width:659px), the analysis graph lands below the fold once a game has moves. Three levers: (1) auto-scroll the nav/hamburger header out of view when the graph appears, (2) relocate the two material displays into the top panel and controls row, (3) reduce vertical floors/margins in the mobile column.
design:
# Mobile portrait: reclaim vertical space so the analysis graph is in view ## Context On `/play` in mobile portrait (`@media max-width: 659px`), the single-column grid stacks `panel → board → notices → moves → graph`. The board fills ~100vw and `.moves-column` carries two `MaterialDisplay` rows above/below the move list, so the analysis graph lands below the fold once a game has moves. Goal: get at least part of the graph in view without a long scroll. Three confirmed levers: (1) auto-scroll the nav/hamburger header out of view when the graph appears, (2) relocate the two material displays into the top panel + controls row, always in portrait, (3) trim vertical margins. This revision incorporates review findings (no-op CSS, missing flex rules, prop-contract typing, scroll state machine, ControlsRow guard, real vertical budget, stale e2e). ## Key facts verified during planning - Mobile move list is **HorizontalMoveList** (`AnalysisConnectors.tsx:317`, `useMediaQuery(GAME_MOBILE_QUERY)`, query = `max-width:659px`). It renders `` (`src/components/ControlsRow.tsx`) above the strip. - **The original moves-column floor is already overridden on mobile.** `src/App.css:7883` (`.moves-column:has(.h-move-list)`) sets `min-height:0; max-height:none`. So changing the `280px`/clamp at `:7870` is a **no-op** — dropped from this plan. The real wins are removing the two material rows and scrolling the nav away. - `HorizontalMoveList` is typed with the **shared `MoveListProps`** (`MoveList.tsx:20`, `HorizontalMoveList.tsx:41`) — new material props must be added there or TS won't compile. - Both flex containers **wrap**: `.chess-panel` (`App.css:7654`, `flex-wrap:wrap`, children use explicit `order`) and `.controls-row` (`App.css:5346`, `flex-wrap:wrap`). Capture-heavy material can force a new wrap row and negate savings unless constrained. - The e2e `e2e/mobile-game-layout.spec.ts` (committed 2026-04-27) **predates** HorizontalMoveList (2026-06-06) and still polls `.move-list-grid .move-button` / asserts `.move-list-nav`/`.move-list-scroll` at 360px — those no longer render in portrait, so the spec is stale and must be migrated to horizontal-list selectors as part of this work. ## Vertical budget (after nav scrolled away) Approx heights, portrait, mid-game (no notices): | Region | height | |---|---| | layout top padding | ~4px | | `.chess-panel` (1 row, avatar 36px) | ~44px | | board (`100vw`, eval bar beside) | ~W px (W = viewport width) | | `.moves-column`: ControlsRow + strip row | ~80px | | graph svg (`--game-graph-height`) | 130px | | gaps (≈3 × 6px) | ~18px | - **390×844:** 4+44+~375+80+18 = ~521 → graph bottom ≈ 651. Whole column fits in the viewport, so there may be **no scroll range** and the nav stays put (that's fine — the graph is already visible; see verification note). - **360×640 (tight):** 4+44+~340+80+18 = ~486 → graph bottom ≈ 616 ≤ 640, so the **full** graph is visible with ~24px to spare. **With the two material rows still present (+~56px)** the graph would start at ~542 and bottom at ~672 > 640 → fully off-screen. This is exactly why relocation + scroll (not the no-op floor change) is what makes 360×640 work. Note: this budget excludes the notices row. When review/rehook toasts are present they add a row and push the graph down — graph-visibility should be measured in a **toast-free** mid-game state, separate from the notice-layout assertions. ## Implementation ### 1. Auto-scroll header out of view — `src/components/ChessGame.tsx` - Import `useMediaQuery` + `GAME_MOBILE_QUERY`; add `const isNarrow = useMediaQuery(GAME_MOBILE_QUERY)`. - Add a ref to `.chess-section` (top of the rendered tree). - State machine via `prevHasBelowRef` (a `useRef`): - **First effect run:** seed `prevHasBelowRef.current = hasBelowBoardContent` and do **not** scroll → initial mount with existing moves does **not** auto-scroll (avoids a jarring jump on arrival). - **Subsequent runs:** scroll **once** only on a `false → true` transition of `hasBelowBoardContent` **and** `isNarrow`. Then update the ref. - Analysis-map updates re-render but don't change `hasBelowBoardContent` → no repeat scroll. - Desktop→mobile resize flips `isNarrow` only, not the transition → no scroll. - New game after an earlier game: content clears (`true→false`) then first move (`false→true`) → one scroll. Desired. - Scroll: `sectionRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ block: "start", behavior })` where `behavior = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches ? "auto" : "smooth"`. Because `.nav-bar` precedes `.chess-section` in normal flow, aligning the section top to the viewport scrolls the nav off while keeping panel + board visible; the user scrolls up to reach the hamburger. ### 2. Relocate material (always, portrait) Material can't be CSS-moved across grid containers, so render instances in the targets and hide the originals on mobile. `MaterialDisplay` is `memo`'d. - **Top → panel:** add props `materialFen: string` + `materialPerspective: "white"|"black"` to `GameInfoPanel`; render `
` inside `.chess-panel`. Pass `displayedFen` + `opponentColor` from `ChessGame`. - **Bottom → controls row:** add `materialFen?: string` + `materialPerspective?: "white"|"black"` to **`MoveListProps`** (`MoveList.tsx`, so the shared type compiles), destructure in `HorizontalMoveList`, pass to `ControlsRow` (extend `ControlsRowProps`). Thread the values `ChessGame → ConnectedMoveList` (new props) `→ HorizontalMoveList → ControlsRow`, supplying `displayedFen` + `playerColor`. The vertical `MoveList` ignores the props (desktop material stays in the column). - **ControlsRow guard (review pt 5):** update the early-return at `ControlsRow.tsx:39` to also stay mounted when material is supplied: `if (!(onResign || onFlipBoard || onReset || onRevert || hasAddButton) && !hasMaterial) return null;`. - **Hide originals on mobile:** in the 659px block, `.game-page .moves-column > .material-display { display: none; }`. ### 3. CSS — flex rules + margin trims (`src/App.css`, 659px block) Explicit rules so relocated material never creates a wrap row (review pt 2): - `.chess-panel__material`: shown only in the 659px block (`display:flex` there, `display:none` by default); `order: 2; flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; max-width: 5.5rem; overflow: hidden;`. Reuse the existing `.game-page .material-icons { font-size:26px }` override; add `flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow: hidden` so capture-heavy lists clip rather than wrap. - `.controls-row` (659 block): `flex-wrap: nowrap; min-width: 0;` so the icon buttons keep their size; trailing material wrapper gets `margin-left: auto; flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden;` and clips when captures are many. - Drop fixed `min-height` on the relocated material (let it collapse to the row height) — `MaterialDisplay` already renders no children at 0 captures. - Margin trims: `.app-shell.game-page` padding-top `0.5rem→0.25rem`, gap `0.5rem→0.35rem`; `.chess-layout --game-layout-gap 0.5rem→0.4rem`, `--game-graph-height 140px→130px`. - **Do NOT** touch `.moves-column` min/max-height — already overridden by `:has(.h-move-list)` (review pt 1). ## Files to modify - `src/components/ChessGame.tsx` — scroll effect/ref, thread material props. - `src/components/chess-game/ui/GameInfoPanel.tsx` — top material. - `src/components/MoveList.tsx` — add material props to `MoveListProps`. - `src/components/chess-game/AnalysisConnectors.tsx` — thread props through `ConnectedMoveList` to the move-list component. - `src/components/HorizontalMoveList.tsx` — pass material to `ControlsRow`. - `src/components/ControlsRow.tsx` — accept/render material, fix guard. - `src/App.css` — show/hide + flex rules + margin trims (659 block only). - `e2e/mobile-game-layout.spec.ts` — migrate stale selectors + add assertion. ## Tests - `ChessGame.test.tsx` (review pt 4): mock `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView` and `useMediaQuery`/`matchMedia`; assert (a) exactly **one** scroll on the first `false→true` transition under narrow, (b) **no** scroll on subsequent analysis-only re-renders, (c) **no** scroll when not narrow, (d) **no** scroll on initial mount that already has content, (e) reduced-motion: when `matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")` matches, `scrollIntoView` receives `behavior: "auto"` (else `"smooth"`). - `HorizontalMoveList.test.tsx`: material renders in the controls row when `materialFen` + `materialPerspective` are supplied. - `ControlsRow.test.tsx`: renders when only material is supplied (no actions); still returns null when neither actions nor material present. - `GameInfoPanel.test.tsx`: top material renders from the new props. - `AnalysisConnectors.test.tsx`: new props forwarded to the chosen component. - `breakpoints.test.ts`: unaffected (no breakpoint value change). - `e2e/mobile-game-layout.spec.ts:73`: migrate `.move-list-grid .move-button` / `.move-list-nav` / `.move-list-scroll` to the horizontal equivalents (`.h-move`, `.h-move-list__row`, `.controls-row`). Keep the existing notice-layout assertions (which depend on the seeded review/rehook toasts) in their own scenario. Add a **separate, toast-free** mid-game scenario for graph visibility: after playing moves + auto-scroll, **poll the `.analysis-graph` bounding box** (not the `.chess-graph-area` wrapper — the wrapper can intersect while the graph sits below it) until it intersects the viewport (`y < viewport.height && y + height > 0`); polling absorbs the async smooth scroll. Cover 390×844 and 360×640. ## Verification - `npm run build` — confirms the shared-`MoveListProps` change type-checks end to end (review pt 3). - `npm run test -- ChessGame ControlsRow HorizontalMoveList GameInfoPanel AnalysisConnectors` (run named files in isolation per the flaky pre-push note). - `npx playwright test e2e/mobile-game-layout.spec.ts`. - Manual (`/run` or dev server, portrait ≤659px, check both 390×844 and 360×640): 1. Play moves so the graph mounts → the page scrolls as far as the available range allows (the nav scrolls off when there's range; at 390×844 the column may fit entirely with no scroll range, which is fine). Require only that the `.analysis-graph` is visible in the viewport. 2. Opponent captures appear in the top panel, player captures in the controls row; neither duplicated; capture-heavy lists clip without adding a row. 3. Desktop (>659px) unchanged — material in the moves column, no auto-scroll. 4. Scroll up → hamburger still reachable/functional.
notes: Implemented: (1) auto-scroll effect in ChessGame.tsx (false→true transition of hasBelowBoardContent, narrow only, reduced-motion aware, seeds on first run); (2) material relocated — opponent captures → GameInfoPanel chess-panel__material, player captures → ControlsRow controls-row__material via MoveListProps/ConnectedMoveList threading; (3) CSS 659px block: show relocated material + nowrap flex rules, hide moves-column originals, margin trims (padding/gap/graph-height 140→130). Tests added/updated: ChessGame (scroll once narrow / no-scroll desktop), ControlsRow (material-only render + null guard), HorizontalMoveList (controls-row material), AnalysisConnectors (forwarding). e2e spec migrated stale move-list-* selectors to h-move/controls-row + new toast-free graph-visibility scenario (390x844, 360x640, stable user). Build typechecks; 93 unit tests pass. e2e not run (needs live server). Not committed pending review.

title: Fix intermittent 'Invalid move e2e4' on drill opening (re-entrancy race)
description: The opening opponent-move effect in ChessGame.tsx fires applyOpponentMove without an in-flight guard. Because applyOpponentMove is async (backend round-trip) and the guard conditions (moveCount===0 && turn==='w') hold during the await, the effect re-runs on volatile dep changes (isThinking/engineStatus/isViewingLive) and launches a second concurrent request. One applies the ghost move (e4); the other falls back to the local engine and tries e2e4 on a board where white already moved, throwing 'Invalid move: {from:e2,to:e4}'. Add a re-entrancy guard ref so the opening move fires once.
